details: CONFIRMED by reading. `_close_orphan` (relay_queue.py:1534-1554) refuses only when the item is not taken or its branch is live,
then `test_refusal(main, master, test)`, which checks only that a test of that name is defined in the file on master. It never
runs the test and never reads a check. The project rule (rules/queue.md:21) is that a fix closes with its test and the branch's
check (`relay queue done` on the branch, `close_refusal`), or with `--fixed-by`, where "relay runs the test at the commit's
parent and at the commit: it must fail, then pass". The merge hook's step_queue enforces the first for merges; queue commits
land straight on master through `_run`, so nothing guards this path. `close_fixed_by` (relay_queue.py:1193) already closes a
fix "taken by a branch that is merged or gone ... keeping its take" from the main checkout, with that proof. So the new path
is a weaker copy of an existing one, and it opens a way to mark any orphaned fix as done (an abandoned branch included; the
docstring itself says "merged or gone"). The incident's real defect was that the from-main refusal "done runs in the worktree
of the task branch that took the item" did not name `--fixed-by` or `release` (principle 10: a refusal names the next step).
Size: 15 agent minutes (replace `_close_orphan` with a refusal naming both commands, rewrite test_o1/o2 to that, keep o3/o4).
evidence: sed -n 1534,1554p lib/relay_queue.py: planner checks state == taken, not _branch_live, test_refusal(main, refs/heads/master, test); then closes.
sed -n 1193,1199p lib/relay_queue.py: close_fixed_by "An item taken by a branch that is merged or gone is closed here, keeping its take"
git log -S"An item taken by a branch that is merged or gone" -- lib/relay_queue.py: f34a48d1 2026-10-25 queue: close a fix that another change already fixed (--fixed-by)

rules/queue.md:21: "`relay queue done` to close a fix with its test and the branch's check ... `relay queue done <fix> --fixed-by <commit> --test ...` ... (relay runs the test at the commit's parent and at the commit: it must fail, then pass)"
failing_case: Queue item `job` (fix) taken by wt/gone; wt/gone was deleted without being merged (abandoned, nothing fixed). From the main
checkout: `relay queue done job --test tests/test_queue.py::<any existing test>`.
Now: the item is closed as done (state done, test = that name), committed to master; nothing ran, no check was read.
Should: refuse, naming the ways that carry proof: `relay queue done job --fixed-by <commit> --test <file>.py::<Class>::<name>`
(test fails at the commit's parent and passes at the commit) for a fix that landed, or `relay queue release job` for one that did not.
fix_hint: In `done`, when the branch is the default branch, raise Refused: "from the main checkout a fix taken by a branch that is
merged or gone closes with relay queue done <slug> --fixed-by <commit> --test <file>.py::<Class>::<name>; one that was never
fixed is released with relay queue release <slug>" (keep the live-branch refusal of test_o3). Drop `_close_orphan`.
pass_cases: 1. Fix item taken by wt/gone (no such branch), main checkout, `done(main, "job", "tests/test_job.py::test_job")` with no
proof that the test fixed anything: Refused; the message names `--fixed-by <commit> --test` and `relay queue release job`;
the item stays taken.
2. Same item, `close_fixed_by(main, "job", <commit>, "tests/test_job.py::test_job")` where the test fails at the commit's
parent and passes at the commit: state done, taken_by wt/gone kept, fixed_by = that sha (works today, test_queue_close).
3. Same item, `release(main, "job")`: state open (works today, test_o4).
4. Item taken by a live unmerged branch wt/live, done from main: Refused naming wt/live (as test_o3 today).
5. If instead the fix keeps a from-main `done`: it closes only when the landed tip of wt/gone (found on master) carries a
check of the item with Q1 MET (`close_refusal(main, <tip>, slug, test)` is None); an abandoned branch with no such check is refused.
reason: tests/test_queue.py:1442 test_o1 passes; fails at 652ce7c0; o3 and o4 pass. _close_orphan dropped.
findings.summary: done from the main checkout closes a fix item with no proof: no check with Q1 MET, no test run, only a test name that exists on master

details: CONFIRMED: `open_item_refusal(tree, branch)` reads `held_fix_items(worktree)`, which reads the queue at the worktree's HEAD.
It runs in land() before `_locked` takes master into the branch. A take on master that the branch has not merged (relay queue
take merges at once, but its merge can fail and be aborted, and test_f4 builds exactly this state) is invisible, the landing
goes through, and the fix stays taken by a deleted branch. test_f4 now asserts that outcome as correct.
Size: 15 agent minutes (read the items taken by the branch from the default branch too, e.g. items on master with
taken_by == branch that are not closed at the branch head; change test_f4's fix half to expect the refusal, or move it to a
fix item closed on the branch).
evidence: tests/test_land.py:579-585: master_commit fx taken by wt/x; land returncode 0; assertEqual(queue["fx"]["state"], "taken")
lib/relay_land.py:279-280: tree = _preflight(...); open_item_refusal(tree, branch) before lock and before take() in _locked
failing_case: Existing test tests/test_land.py:576 test_f4_landing_closes_the_feature_item_not_the_fix: master gets fx.json (fix, taken by
wt/x) after wt/x forked; `relay land wt/x`.
Now: exit 0, master advances, and the test asserts queue["fx"]["state"] == "taken" after the landing: the very outcome the
item reports (a fix left taken by a branch that is gone). The refusal ran on wt/x's HEAD before `take` merged master in.
Should: exit 2 naming `relay queue done fx -C <worktree> --test ...`, master unchanged.
fix_hint: In open_item_refusal, also list the fix items that the default branch shows taken by `branch` and that are not closed at the
branch head (Reader(main, refs/heads/<default>)), or call it again after `take` inside _locked. Update test_f4 accordingly.
pass_cases: 1. test_f4 set-up (fx taken by wt/x committed on master only, not in wt/x's head): relay land wt/x exits 2, output holds
"relay queue done fx -C <wt> --test", master unchanged, no gate run.
2. The feature half of test_f4 (feat taken by wt/x, no fix item): land exits 0 and feat is done with evidence (as today).
3. Item taken by wt/x inside the branch head (test_land_refuses_a_branch_whose_taken_fix_item_is_still_open): exit 2 (as today).
4. Branch with no item: exit 0 (test_land_of_a_branch_with_no_item_is_not_refused_for_one).
findings.summary: land checks for an open item at the branch head before the take of master, so an item whose take is on master but not yet in the branch lands and stays taken
